name: CFML
title: CFML (2025)

presenceList.meta: R2, Ec6, Ec7, D3, S1, S2, Q2, Q3

type.text: **A variable is dynamically typed**: A name takes any value
**A component method resolves at run time**: A dynamic call reaches a method by name
**A variable can be undefined**: The type does not carry the check
**There is no sum type**: A component or a struct carries a discriminator, and a `switch` is not checked

construction.text: **A component is a class**: `init` is the constructor
**The application and session scopes are global**: A value in `application` is reachable from every request

memory.text: **There is no scope-exit release**: A file or a query is closed by hand

error.text: **An error can be ignored**: A failed tag returns false
**There is no result type**: A failure is an exception, and a success is a return value

concurrency.text: **`cfthread` starts an asynchronous task**: The engine scopes the thread to the request
**Shared scopes are the default**: `application` and `session` are reachable from every thread
**A lock is manual**: `cflock` is the discipline, and nothing detects a missing one

platform.text: **The runtime is a JVM servlet**: A CFML application deploys to Tomcat or a Java EE server
**The language has more than one implementation**: Adobe ColdFusion and Lucee run the same source

performance.text: **A collection pause is part of the timing**
**A compiled template is cached**: The engine compiles a page once and reuses it

ecosystem.text: **Two engines dominate**: Adobe ColdFusion and Lucee are the choices
**A large body of tag-era code remains**: A 2005 application still runs
**A Java library is reachable**: A component calls a JAR directly

evolution.text: **A release is annual**: A named release ships with updates
**The tag and the script syntax both remain**: New code can use either

domain.text: **The engine sets the architecture**: `Application.cfc` and the scopes decide the structure
**A data-driven web application is the ordinary project**: A form, a query, and a page

learning.text: **The tag syntax is approachable**: An HTML-like page reads as markup

syntax.text: **The tag syntax is verbose**: `<cfquery>`, `<cfoutput>`, and a closing tag
**Two syntaxes share one language**: Tags and CFScript state the same construct

testing.text: **A test framework exists**: TestBox runs a unit and an integration test

security.text: **`evaluate()` and `cfexecute` are ordinary calls**: Text becomes code or a command
**Output is not escaped by default**: A value is written as it is, and `encodeForHTML` is the caller's call
**A dynamically typed value is checked at run time**: A wrong type fails when the line runs

reproducibility.text: **A deployment copies source**: The artifact is the source tree, not a verified build

supplychain.text: **A package is installed without a signature check**

observability.text: **There is no open tracing standard in the language**

tradeoffs: **A page is the program**: The request lifecycle is the framework, and the scopes are the state
**Two syntaxes, one language**: A tag and a script statement do the same thing
**The JVM is the platform**: A Java library is one call away, and the GC is the JVM's
**The engine is the deployment**: A CFML application is a directory of templates on a servlet container
verdict: CFML is a dynamic web language on the JVM: components, tags, and the request scopes make a data-driven page cheap, and the Java runtime is behind it. What it charges is the dynamic type, the shared application scope, the manual lock, the tag verbosity, and a two-syntax language whose engines disagree at the edges. Main strength: a fast path from a form to a working page. Main weakness: the scopes and the lock are the program's discipline.

energy.text: No independent energy or time benchmark for the language is recorded.

ai-readiness.text: Sparse public training data: models write it less reliably than a mainstream language [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.
